children: Vail Resorts Inc reported fiscal 2026 results with revenue of $2.84B and diluted EPS of $4.12, down from $2.96B and $7.53 in fiscal 2025 as net income fell to $147.54M from $280M amid softer winter visitation and lower ancillary spend.
¹ Reported as “Total net revenue”. ² Reported as “Net income attributable to Vail Resorts, Inc.”. ³ Reported as “Diluted net income per share attributable to Vail Resorts, Inc.”.
Revenue and visitation impact: Resort revenue declined in FY26 driven by a 13% drop in skier visits following record-low snowfall and warmer temperatures, which reduced ancillary spending.
Pass product momentum: Pass revenue increased by about $38.8M and made up roughly 70% of lift revenue, supporting pre-season cash flow and customer loyalty.
Operational cost actions: RET initiatives produced $45M of savings (before one-time costs), lowering labor and variable expenses.
Lodging and ancillary shift: Lodging RevPAR and managed condo demand fell amid ski-season softness, partially offset by stronger GTLC summer demand.
Real estate activity: Real estate results were volatile in FY26, with parcel sales and timing-driven gains affecting segment EBITDA.
